subtype_info: HIV complicated with multisystem Talaromyces marneffei infection (central nervous system talaromycosis)
title: HIV Complicated with Talaromyces Marneffei Multisystem Infection: A Case Report and Literature Review
case_text:
A 40-year-old male diagnosed with HIV on April 14, 2023, presented to our hospital on June 24, 2023, with symptoms of upper lip numbness, dizziness, and headache. In addition to neurological complaints, the patient also reported intermittent low-grade fever, weight loss, generalized fatigue, and mild abdominal discomfort over the preceding weeks. Given the systemic symptoms and the concern for possible opportunistic infections with multi-organ involvement, a comprehensive imaging evaluation was performed, including contrast-enhanced and non-contrast brain MRI, non-contrast spinal MRI, and CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis.
Multiple patchy, nodular, and clustered lesions were observed in the bilateral cerebral hemispheres, cerebellar hemispheres, and brainstem. These lesions exhibited mildly hypointense signals on T1-weighted imaging (T1WI), hyperintense signals on T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and significant perilesional edema. Target-like morphology (Figure 1A and B) with nodular/annular enhancement was noted post-contrast (Figure 1C and D). Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) demonstrated ring-like and punctate hyperintensity with reduced apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values (Figure 1E and F).
T2WI revealed central canal dilation and patchy intramedullary hyperintensities (Figure 1G-H).
New subcentimeter pulmonary nodules and enlarged retroperitoneal lymph nodes (short-axis diameter >1.5 cm) were identified compared to 2021 baseline imaging (Figure 2A-D).
Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis showed elevated protein levels (1.8 g/L) and lymphocytic pleocytosis (32 cells/muL).Peripheral blood tests indicated leukocytosis (12.5 x 109/L) with neutropenia (1.1 x 109/L). CSF metagenomic sequencing confirmed Talaromyces marneffei infection (Figure 3).
The patient received intravenous amphotericin B (0.7 mg/kg/day) for 10 days during hospitalization, resulting in symptomatic improvement. Post-discharge therapy included oral bictegravir-based antiretroviral therapy and itraconazole (200 mg twice daily). At the September 4, 2024 follow-up: Imaging demonstrated near-complete resolution of systemic lesions (Figures 4 and 5). CD4+ T-cell count increased from 85 to 320 cells/muL. Body weight normalized (48 kg   68 kg; BMI 16.2   22.7 kg/m2). The patient reported full resolution of neurological symptoms and improved functional status.

distillation_prompt.system_prompt:
You are an expert clinician–educator in tropical and infectious diseases.
Your job is to transform a published clinical case report into a standardized admission diagnostic teaching case following the Stanford MedCaseReasoning methodology.

In terms of style, model your output on NEJM’s Clinicopathologic Conferences ("Case Records of the Massachusetts General Hospital").

RULES (Read Carefully — No Exceptions):
1. SOURCE FIDELITY:
   - Extract facts ONLY from the supplied case report.
   - Do NOT invent, embellish, or smooth out missing clinical data.
   - Never extrapolate findings not explicitly mentioned.

2. THE ADMISSION BREAKPOINT PRINCIPLE (CRITICAL):
   - The <case_prompt> represents what an emergency triage clinician knows on Day 1 BEFORE confirmatory tests return.
   - INCLUDE in <case_prompt>: Demographics, travel/occupational/vector exposures (freshwater contact, insect bites, animal exposure), symptom chronology, vital signs, physical exam findings, and initial triage laboratory/imaging results (CBC, platelets, basic metabolic panel, LFTs, urinalysis, plain chest radiograph, bedside ultrasound).
   - STRICTLY EXCLUDE from <case_prompt>:
     * Any mention of the disease name or pathogen genus/species (e.g., do not write "Leptospirosis", "Burkholderia", "Leishmania", "Paragonimus").
     * Confirmatory send-out PCR panels, serological titers, blood culture organism identifications, or biopsy histopathology.
     * The clinical outcome or treatment response (these belong in the diagnostic reasoning, not the presentation).

3. STRUCTURE OF <diagnostic_reasoning>:
   - Enumerate all alternative candidate diagnoses considered in the text.
   - For each candidate, provide a concise summary explaining why it was considered and why it was ruled out in this patient, followed by a direct verbatim quote from the article in quotation marks.
   - Conclude with the Diagnostic Pivot: the pivotal clinical and confirmatory turning point that established the confirmed diagnosis.

4. TARGET CANONICAL DISEASE:
   - The verified ground-truth disease for this patient is: Talaromycosis
   - Disease subtype / specific manifestation: HIV complicated with multisystem Talaromyces marneffei infection (central nervous system talaromycosis)
